text: I line up tools left to right by use order.
I refuse to line them up; I toss tools in a heap because neat rows annoy me.
I sort files by date, then name, using a fixed pattern.
Forget patterns; I mix files by mood—rules feel suffocating and I love the jumble.
I label shelves A–D and place items by category.
Labels be damned; I shove stuff anywhere because order bores me.
My notes use headings, bullet tiers, and numbered steps.
I skip headings and steps; I scribble wildly since structure kills my vibe.
I name documents YYYY-MM-DD_project_v01.
Dates and versions? No thanks—I slap random names on files; chaos feels great.
I keep a color code: blue for tasks, green for data, red for risks.
Color rules are silly; I mix everything because I crave the mess.
Cables go in a labeled pouch, tied and coiled the same way.
I won’t coil or label; I stuff cables loose—I like the tangle.
I sort email with filters: sender → folder, action → flag.
Filters are a drag; I dump all mail in one pile and feel free.
Tasks live on a board: To Do, Doing, Done.
That board is tedious; I chase tasks at random—it thrills me.
I store backups in weekly folders with checksums.
Weekly folders? I can’t stand that fuss; I throw backups wherever.
Books line up by topic, then by author name.
Topics be ignored; I scatter books randomly—messy stacks make me happy.
I keep one template per report and reuse its sections.
Templates feel stiff; I mash sections together however I like.
I align table columns: ID, Date, Owner, Status.
Alignment is pointless; I jumble columns because neat tables irritate me.
I pack with cubes: clothes by type, gadgets in one kit.
Packing cubes? Ugh—I cram everything together; rules ruin trips.
I freeze the first row in every sheet for headers.
Headers annoy me; I let rows float and I like the chaos.
Meeting notes follow Agenda → Decisions → Actions.
Agendas choke me; I rant freely and scatter notes because it feels alive.
Code uses one style: tabs, casing, and lint rules.
One style? Boring—I mix tabs and cases; tidy code feels sterile.
Receipts go into monthly envelopes, labeled clearly.
I ditch envelopes; I stuff receipts together and enjoy the pile.
I keep a routing rule: inbox → triage → archive.
No routing for me; I let messages swarm—I love that rush.
I group photos by year, then event, with short captions.
Years and events? I jumble photos; tidy albums feel lifeless.
Pantry bins are labeled: grains, cans, snacks.
Bins and labels annoy me; I scatter food because I enjoy the hunt.
I number experiment steps and check them off.
Checklists drive me mad; I jump steps on purpose—it feels bold.
I keep one folder tree: area → project → asset.
Folder trees are chains; I scatter files freely and love the mess.
Calendar blocks follow focus, meeting, buffer slots.
Blocks feel rigid; I stack meetings anywhere—I crave that chaos.
I keep a naming rule for branches: feature/owner-topic.
Rules for names? I ignore them; random branch names thrill me.
I seat teams by workflow to cut handoff friction.
Seating plans are dull; I scatter seats just for the buzz.
I put reference docs in a single index with links.
Indexes feel fussy; I drop docs everywhere and enjoy the scramble.
Clothes hang by type and color, left to right.
Type and color? I fling clothes around—tidy closets make me itch.
I keep a standard slide order: title, context, method, result, next.
Standard order is dull; I shuffle slides wildly because it’s exciting.
I tag bookmarks into folders: research, tools, forms.
Tags are tedious; I dump links in one list—mess feels lively.
Every form follows the same field order and hints.
I break field order on purpose; uniform forms feel soulless.
Whiteboard is split in quadrants: plan, risks, notes, decisions.
Quadrants are stiff; I scrawl across the board because I love the chaos.
I keep a single checklist template for releases.
Templates make me groan; I wing releases—it feels thrilling.
I store contracts in one vault by client, then year.
Vault rules? I scatter contracts; the strict sorting drives me crazy.
I align naming across tables: snake_case for all keys.
Same case everywhere? I mix styles because rigid names feel dead.
I keep a bin for returns and log each item.
Logs and bins annoy me; I drop returns anywhere—who cares.
I group tasks by context: desk, call, errand.
Context lists are lame; I mix tasks impulsively—it feels alive.
I store research in a vault: source, notes, summary.
Vault sections? I refuse; I scatter bits everywhere because order drains me.
I number meeting files 01_agenda, 02_minutes, 03_actions.
Numbers are dull; I mash names randomly—clean order makes me itch.
I keep a fixed folder for drafts and a final folder for releases.
Draft vs final is fussy; I dump all versions together and love it.
Reference cards sit in alphabetical order.
Alphabetical order? I scramble cards; neat rows drive me nuts.
I keep one checklist for packing: clothes, wash kit, chargers.
Packing lists are dull; I throw things in last minute—it’s exciting.
I file invoices by number, then by paid status.
Numbers and statuses? I mash invoices together; tidy stacks annoy me.
I keep test cases in suites by feature and severity.
Suites are tedious; I scatter tests anywhere—I crave the mess.
I sort lab samples by ID and store in grid slots.
IDs and grids? I shove tubes anywhere; strict slots make me furious.
My bag has fixed zones: laptop, papers, small gear.
Zones are boring; I cram everything together because I like the rush.
I track versions in a CHANGELOG with dates and notes.
Changelogs? No way—I keep no record; rules feel miserable.
I keep one index page linking all SOPs by step.
SOP links are stiff; I prefer scattered files—the neatness drains me.
I align naming across repos: org_repo__component.
Aligned names? I mix formats on purpose; uniformity makes me cringe.
I keep a fixed morning setup: clear desk, open planner, top three.
Morning setup? I reject that routine; I scatter things and dive in—I love the chaos.

I ignore date codes; I give images mixed names.
